title: AI agents can browse the web. Now they need a way to pay for it.

content_html:
TL;DR

AI agents increasingly need to make purchases, but today’s payment systems assume a human is involved. The Linux Foundation’s x402 initiative, backed by over 40 organizations including Visa, Mastercard, and Stripe, aims to create internet-native payments for software. Casper Network has upgraded its csprUSD stablecoin for x402 micropayments. Whether blockchain or traditional rails win, the infrastructure for machine-to-machine commerce is being built now.

For the past two years, the AI industry has focused on making models smarter. Every new release promises better reasoning, longer context windows, or more capable autonomous agents. Increasingly, people assume that software won’t just answer questions; it will also complete tasks for us. This raises a concern that has received far less attention: what happens when those agents need to make a purchase?

A travel assistant might need to pay for access to a premium flight database. A coding agent could rent computing power for a few minutes to run a complex workload. A research assistant may need to unlock a paywalled paper or buy access to a proprietary API. None of these transactions require a human decision at the moment. They just need to happen quickly enough for the software to keep working.

Today’s payment systems were not designed with this in mind.

Most online commerce still assumes that a person is involved somewhere in the process. Credit cards need names, billing addresses, and authentication. Subscription services expect someone to consciously sign up and then decide whether to renew each month. Even digital wallets generally require a human to approve a transaction before money moves. These assumptions create issues when the customer is software making thousands of low-value purchasing decisions every hour.

The economics are tricky too. Charging $20 a month for API access makes sense when the customer is a business or an individual. It makes much less sense when an AI agent only needs a single request that costs a small fraction of a cent. Charging by the request seems like an obvious solution, but existing payment systems were never built for transactions that small, frequent, or automated. This challenge is beginning to draw serious attention outside the crypto industry.

Earlier this month, the Linux Foundation announced the launch of the x402 Foundation, an initiative supported by over 40 organizations, including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Google, AWS, Stripe, Coinbase, Circle, and Cloudflare. The goal is to create a common standard for internet-native payments that software can initiate automatically, using the long-unused HTTP 402 “Payment Required” status code as the basis for machine-to-machine commerce.

The list of participants is notable for bringing together companies that rarely come together on emerging technologies. Payment networks, cloud providers, blockchain firms, and internet infrastructure companies are all recognizing the same problem. If AI agents become important players in the digital economy, they need a way to exchange value as naturally as they exchange information.

For blockchain networks, this presents a different chance than what they sought in the last decade. Much of crypto’s early ambition focused on replacing current financial systems or convincing consumers to pay with digital assets. Adoption has been slower than many anticipated, mainly because traditional payment systems already work reasonably well for most people. Software has different priorities.

An AI agent does not care whether a payment goes through a familiar banking interface or a blockchain network. It cares whether the payment settles reliably, whether the cost is predictable, and whether the fee is low enough that it does not outweigh the value of the transaction itself.

This shift helps explain why some blockchain projects are beginning to focus on AI infrastructure rather than consumer payments. Casper Network is one of them. Today, the network announced an upgraded version of its dollar-backed stablecoin, csprUSD, which is meant to serve as the default settlement asset for AI agents using x402 payment flows on Casper.

According to the announcement, the upgrade makes it compatible with Casper 2.0 and CEP-3009, the network’s standard for authorized transfers. This allows payment authorizations to be signed off-chain and settled on-chain as part of a standard HTTP request. The network has also reduced minimum transaction costs to make low-value machine payments economically viable, while integrating its ProofLayer infrastructure to provide proof of collateral and redemption activity.

On its own, another stablecoin launch would likely struggle to stand out in a market that already has hundreds of them. However, viewed through the lens of AI, this announcement reflects a broader shift happening across the industry. Stablecoins are increasingly being discussed not just as trading tools or payment options for people, but as operating infrastructure for software. If AI agents become regular users of online services, they will need access to stable digital assets that can move automatically, settle quickly, and integrate directly into internet protocols.

Whether blockchain ultimately becomes the leading foundation for those payments is still uncertain. The involvement of companies like Visa, Mastercard, and Stripe suggests that traditional financial systems will play a significant role alongside crypto-native systems. The eventual framework will likely combine elements from both, especially if developers prioritize compatibility over ideological preferences. The underlying trend itself is becoming harder to ignore.

The conversation around AI has mainly focused on intelligence, reasoning, and productivity. Yet these abilities only become commercially useful when software can engage in the economy without constant human oversight. Buying data, paying for computers, accessing digital services, and compensating other software will likely become routine for autonomous systems.

If that happens, the challenge will not only be building smarter AI. It will be creating an internet where software can transact as easily as it communicates. This may become one of the more important infrastructure debates in the next phase of AI, even if it attracts less attention than the models themselves.

sentences.en: It will be creating an internet where software can transact as easily as it communicates.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

人工智能代理越来越需要进行购买，但当今的支付系统假设有人参与。 Linux 基金会的 x402 计划得到了 Visa、Mastercard 和 Stripe 等 40 多个组织的支持，旨在为软件创建互联网原生支付。 Casper Network 已将其 csprUSD 稳定币升级为 x402 小额支付。 无论区块链还是传统铁路获胜，机器对机器商务的基础设施现在正在建设中。

过去两年，人工智能行业一直致力于让模型变得更加智能。 每个新版本都承诺更好的推理、更长的上下文窗口或更强大的自主代理。 人们越来越多地认为软件不仅能回答问题，还能解决问题。它还将为我们完成任务。 这就引发了一个很少受到关注的问题：当这些代理商需要购买时会发生什么？

旅行助理可能需要付费才能访问高级航班数据库。 编码代理可以租用几分钟的计算能力来运行复杂的工作负载。 研究助理可能需要解锁付费论文或购买专有 API 的访问权限。 目前这些交易都不需要人工决定。 它们只需要发生得足够快，以便软件能够继续工作。

今天的支付系统在设计时并未考虑到这一点。

大多数在线商务仍然假设有人参与该过程的某个地方。 信用卡需要姓名、帐单地址和身份验证。 订阅服务希望有人有意识地注册，然后决定每月是否续订。 即使是数字钱包通常也需要人在资金转移之前批准交易。 当客户每小时做出数千个低价值购买决策时，这些假设就会产生问题。

经济学也很棘手。 当客户是企业或个人时，每月收取 20 美元的 API 访问费用是有意义的。 当人工智能代理只需要花费一小部分钱的单个请求时，它的意义就小得多。 按请求收费似乎是一个显而易见的解决方案，但现有的支付系统从来都不是为小额、频繁或自动化的交易而构建的。 这一挑战开始引起加密行业之外的严重关注。

本月早些时候，Linux 基金会宣布推出 x402 基金会，该计划得到了 40 多个组织的支持，包括 Visa、Mastercard、American Express、Google、AWS、Stripe、Coinbase、Circle 和 Cloudflare。 目标是为软件可以自动启动的互联网原生支付创建一个通用标准，使用长期未使用的 HTTP 402“需要支付”状态代码作为机器对机器商务的基础。

参与者名单中值得注意的是，他们将很少在新兴技术上聚集在一起的公司聚集在一起。 支付网络、云提供商、区块链公司和互联网基础设施公司都认识到同样的问题。 如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的重要参与者，他们需要一种像交换信息一样自然地交换价值的方式。

对于区块链网络来说，这提供了与他们在过去十年中寻求的不同的机会。 加密货币的早期雄心主要集中在取代当前的金融系统或说服消费者使用数字资产支付。 采用速度比许多人预期的要慢，主要是因为传统支付系统对于大多数人来说已经相当有效。 软件有不同的优先级。

人工智能代理并不关心付款是通过熟悉的银行界面还是区块链网络进行。 它关心支付是否可靠地结算，成本是否可预测，以及费用是否足够低以至于不会超过交易本身的价值。

这种转变有助于解释为什么一些区块链项目开始关注人工智能基础设施而不是消费者支付。 Casper 网络就是其中之一。 今天，该网络宣布了其美元支持的稳定币 csprUSD 的升级版本，该稳定币旨在作为 Casper 上使用 x402 支付流的人工智能代理的默认结算资产。

根据公告，此次升级使其兼容 Casper 2.0 和 CEP-3009（该网络的授权传输标准）。 这允许支付授权作为标准 HTTP 请求的一部分在链外签名并在链上结算。 该网络还降低了最低交易成本，使低价值机器支付在经济上可行，同时集成其 ProofLayer 基础设施以提供抵押品和赎回活动的证明。

就其本身而言，再推出一款稳定币可能很难在已经拥有数百种稳定币的市场中脱颖而出。 然而，从人工智能的角度来看，这一公告反映了整个行业正在发生的更广泛的转变。 人们越来越多地讨论稳定币，不仅将其视为人们的交易工具或支付选项，而且将其视为软件的运营基础设施。 如果人工智能代理成为在线服务的常规用户，他们将需要访问稳定的数字资产，这些资产可以自动移动、快速结算并直接集成到互联网协议中。

区块链是否最终成为这些支付的主要基础仍不确定。 Visa、Mastercard 和 Stripe 等公司的参与表明，传统金融系统将与加密原生系统一起发挥重要作用。 最终的框架可能会结合两者的元素，特别是如果开发人员优先考虑兼容性而不是意识形态偏好的话。 潜在趋势本身正变得越来越难以忽视。

围绕人工智能的讨论主要集中在智能、推理和生产力方面。 然而，只有当软件能够在没有持续人类监督的情况下参与经济时，这些能力才变得具有商业用途。 购买数据、购买计算机、访问数字服务以及补偿其他软件可能会成为自治系统的例行公事。

如果发生这种情况，挑战将不仅仅是构建更智能的人工智能。 它将创建一个互联网，让软件可以像通信一样轻松地进行交易。 这可能成为人工智能下一阶段中更重要的基础设施争论之一，即使它比模型本身吸引的注意力要少。
